    s = ''.join([char for char in s if char not in c])
    return (s,s[::-1] == s)

def test_reverse_delete():
    # Basic case: delete chars, result is not a palindrome
    assert reverse_delete("abcde", "ae") == ("bcd", False)
    
    # Delete one char, result not a palindrome
    assert reverse_delete("abcdef", "b") == ("acdef", False)
    
    # Result is a palindrome
    assert reverse_delete("abcdedcba", "ab") == ("cdedc", True)
    
    # All chars deleted, empty string is a palindrome
    assert reverse_delete("abc", "abc") == ("", True)
    
    # No chars deleted (c has no matching chars)
    assert reverse_delete("hello", "xyz") == ("hello", False)
    
    # Empty c: string unchanged, palindrome check on original
    assert reverse_delete("racecar", "") == ("racecar", True)
    assert reverse_delete("hello", "") == ("hello", False)
    
    # Deleting chars results in a palindrome
    assert reverse_delete("abccba", "a") == ("bccb", True)
    assert reverse_delete("abaacdedcaba", "ab") == ("cdedc", True)
    
    # Single character result
    assert reverse_delete("aaa", "a") == ("", True)
    assert reverse_delete("aba", "b") == ("aa", True)
    
    # Case sensitivity check
    assert reverse_delete("AbA", "a") == ("AbA", False)
    
    # Duplicates in c should not affect the result
    assert reverse_delete("abcde", "aae") == ("bcd", False)
    
    # Numeric strings
    assert reverse_delete("12321", "1") == ("232", True)
    assert reverse_delete("12321", "2") == ("131", True)
    
    # String with special characters
    assert reverse_delete("a!b!c!", "!") == ("abc", False)
    
    # Both strings empty
    assert reverse_delete("", "") == ("", True)
    
    # s empty, c non-empty
    assert reverse_delete("", "abc") == ("", True)
